close_reason: Recruitment skips-and-replaces unlockable candidates (ghost registrations from dead node names); director prunes non-layout directory entries after completed recovery. Verified against the user's actual wedged data dir: recovery completes in 561ms and hello reads back world.
description: User's livebook data dir hangs on restart: the coordinator's raft-durable service directory retains registrations from prior sessions, including workers registered by dead node names (livebook mints a fresh node name per runtime, orphaning all prior registrations). Log recruitment treats a ghost as a recruitable candidate, fails to lock it (:unavailable at the dead address), and HALTS the attempt: {:failed_to_lock_recruited_service, id, :unavailable} on every attempt forever. Chicken-and-egg: deregistration requires reconciliation, reconciliation requires a completed recovery, recovery cannot complete because of the ghost. Fix: (1) recruitment treats a lock failure on a candidate the same as the candidate being absent — skip it and create a fresh worker (an attempt is a pure function of its view; the failed lock is the view). (2) After recovery completes and the layout is durable, the director deregisters directory entries the layout does not reference — layout-is-truth extended from local workers to the directory; live-but-stale workers re-register on rejoin and get reconciled locally. WAL/chunks in the user's dir verified healthy; the hello->world chunk is intact.
title: Recovery tolerates ghost directory entries; the director prunes them after completion
